data.narrative:
eleQtron is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Christof Wunderlich, Michael Johanning, and Jan Henrik Leisse, with €50M+ raised to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Valuation analysis relied on a single applicable method: stage-progression. Using the €50M total raised as a proxy base value, application of a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $100M. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable; while 8 same-sector private peers exist, none satisfied narrow same-stage or adjacent-stage filtering criteria necessary to establish a reliable comparable set of three or more datapoints. Deriving a median from the broader sector peer universe would introduce unacceptable selection bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M (low) to $115M (high), with a median of $100M. This range reflects the stage-progression method applied conservatively. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable Series A quantum computing transactions and the nascent, heterogeneous nature of the sector, which limits confidence in standard step-up multipliers. Validation of this range would require either additional peer-stage financials or forward-looking metrics specific to eleQtron's technology differentiation and go-to-market trajectory.
